    How to read this. Margins are final pre-election polling averages (RealClearPolling, Silver Bulletin, On Point Politics, Poliwave and similar), collected Nov 2–3, 2026. Polls close tonight; no results are shown here. "Wall rating" is a synthesis of those averages with Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball ratings, not an official rating. Seat math: Republicans hold 53 seats, Democrats 45 plus 2 independents who caucus with them. 35 seats are up (22 R, 13 D, including specials in Ohio and Florida). Of the 21 not shown, 12 are safe R and 9 safe D.

    Main national sources: Sabato's Crystal Ball final ratings · Forbes: final NYT/Siena polls · RealClearPolling · Silver Bulletin · Poliwave · Fox News Power Rankings · Kalshi · WLRN / NPR races to watch

    The race rack

    Grouped by final rating, from Democratic-leaning to Republican-leaning. Click any race.

    How to read this. 29 of the most competitive races, chosen from Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball, DDHQ, ABC, NPR and Reuters battleground lists as of Nov 2–3, 2026. Ratings are Cook's where we could confirm them; where forecasters disagree, the race is shown as a toss-up and the panel says so. District polling is sparse and often sponsored by a party: those polls are labelled (D) or (R). Seat totals outside the wall are approximate, derived from Cook's late-October count of 220 Democratic-favoured seats. District dots sit at each district's main city because several states (TX, CA, FL, OH, MO, NC, UT, AL) drew new maps for 2026. Photos: official House portraits (public domain, via unitedstates/images) and campaign photos via Ballotpedia.

    National sources: Cook House ratings · The Hill / DDHQ · Washington Post guide · NPR · ABC News · Ballotpedia redistricting · Congress Countdown
